text:
sara-support: Escalating a customer issue for Acme Health — SCIM jobs failing after they rotated SAML attributes. They report user deprovisioning not happening, API 403s for decrypt ops, and gaps in the audit log around the same time. Need SRE/security triage. :rotating_light:

jordan-se: Thanks, Sara. What errors are they seeing on SCIM? Any reproducible steps?

sara-support: Short repro from customer: 1) Update SAML attribute mapping (email -> work_email) in IdP 2) Trigger SCIM sync from our console 3) Observe user still in org and API returns 403 on /v1/provision/decrypt-key. They attached logs.

sara-support: Log excerpt they pasted: ```error: KMSDecrypt failed status=403 client=acme-health org=org_42 key=projects/prod/keys/rlw-01 msg="permission denied"```

sam-eng: Hm 403 on KMS decrypt implies IAM binding mismatch or key access policy change. Did they rotate KMS roles at the same time as SAML?

maria-ps: Customer says they only changed attribute mapping, not KMS. They did note an admin ran an "emergency deprovision" script earlier today — could be linked.

tess-security: Looping in security. @tess-security here. Can you drop the full request ID from the KMS error? We need to check HSM audit and key policy timeline. Also what retention window did they migrate to yesterday?

sara-support: They gave request_id=kjf-3345-a and timestamp ~ 1998887200. Retention migration was toggled by support to 90 days yesterday per compliance request.

kyle-ops: If retention settings changed, audit export jobs might have been reconfigured. But audit gaps plus decrypt 403s smell like a permission sync issue. I'll start by confirming the key IAM bindings for org_42 and check if our KMS proxy returned 403 due to missing mTLS cert.

sam-eng: Quick repro command they ran: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/provision/decrypt-key -d '{"kid":"org_42:rlw-01"}'``` response was `403 Forbidden {"error":"KMS permission denied"}`

maria-ps: Customer is seeing billing spikes too for retries. They want least-privilege review — worried our temporary escalation role might have left broader perms during emergency script run.

tess-security: Action items: 1) Get full audit export for timeframe 1998887000-1998887400 (KMS + provision service) 2) Snapshot key IAM bindings at 1998887200 3) Validate SCIM job logs and token mapping for email->work_email change 4) Temporary mitigation: add scoped fallback role that allows decrypt for deprovision path only (audit all actions).

inc-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421. Assigned to sam-eng, kyle-ops, tess-security. Priority: P1. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0421

sara-support: I've shared the customer's raw logs and their org id in the incident ticket. They've agreed to allow us to run a repro against a staging copy.

kyle-ops: I'll pull the key bindings and KMS proxy logs now. If we see cert/mTLS failures we'll flip to backup proxy and confirm latency impact first.

sam-eng: I'll run a local repro in staging with the exact attribute mapping change and the emergency script to try to reproduce missing deprovision + 403. Will post findings in the incident.

tess-security: Also want legal/ compliance on standby — retention change might have caused export rotation that dropped entries. @maria-ps can you confirm the retention toggle process and whether exports are paused during migration?

maria-ps: Confirmed — retention toggle triggers a short pause (30s-2m) in export workers while indexes are re-sharded. Shouldn't drop events but could re-order them. I'll include that in the incident notes.

sara-support: Customer flagged priority due to HIPAA record removal concerns. They asked for timeline and root cause ASAP.

inc-bot: Update INC-2026-0421: triage started by sam-eng at 1998887780.

tess-security: Next steps: sam/kyle to report repro status and binding snapshot within 2 hours. If reproed, we roll scoped fallback role and replay missing audit events to customer. Keep me tagged in the incident.

sara-support: Thanks all — I'll keep customer updated and share incident link. :pray:
